reasons: Lake identity confirms State v. Mansor, Oregon Supreme Court, decided 2018-06-28.
Lake citations confirm official citation 363 Or. 185, parallel citation 421 P.3d 323, and no vendor-neutral citation.

defect.evidence_quote: We recognize that some of the legal conclusions that we reach in this case likely would have implications for a plain view argument, if raised in a computer search case. However, as noted, the state does not rely on that doctrine here and neither party has briefed the issue; in these circumstances, further discussion regarding the application vel non of that doctrine to computer searches should await a future case.
defect.locator_note: text/State v. Mansor__ee4554.txt p-82; content_page.md homes/Appears on
defect.problem: The Plain View Doctrine home role overstates the case. Mansor discusses possible implications for plain view but expressly says the state did not rely on the doctrine and that application of the doctrine to computer searches should await a future case.
defect.proposed_fix: Do not list Mansor as a Plain View Doctrine recent development. Move it to a computer-warrant particularity/use-restriction home, or label it only as a related reserved plain-view issue.

reasons: The opinion expressly reserves the plain-view computer-search issue rather than deciding it.
The holding is about Article I, section 9 computer-warrant particularity and use of information outside the warrant, not a plain-view holding.
residual_risks: The case can still be cross-referenced from a plain-view page as background or a reserved issue.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: If retained on the Plain View Doctrine page, use a role like 'Related digital-search use restriction; plain-view issue reserved.'

defect.evidence_quote: We also hold that, because of the possibility that a computer search will uncover information that is not authorized by the warrant, a defendant's Article I, section 9, privacy rights prevent the state from using such information unless it comes within an exception to the warrant requirement.
defect.locator_note: content_page.md frontmatter holding; text/State v. Mansor__ee4554.txt p-115
defect.problem: The holding field is clipped and editorialized: it ends at 'that the…' and omits the exception-to-warrant-requirement limitation. The intended rule is supported, but the field as written is incomplete.
defect.proposed_fix: Replace with: 'Decided under Article I, section 9 of the Oregon Constitution: when the state conducts a warranted computer search, it may not use information the warrant did not authorize it to search for unless an exception to the warrant requirement applies.'

reasons: The Article I, section 9 basis is supported by the opinion and lake scope note.
The use restriction is supported, but only with the omitted warrant-exception qualifier.
residual_risks: The current body text mostly states the rule correctly; the defect is concentrated in the frontmatter holding field.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Use sentence-case 'Oregon' and 'use' unless the capitalization is part of a corpus convention.

reasons: The treatment payload matches the lake treatment fields: field_i_validity good_law, as_of_content 2018-06-28, as_of_treatment 2026-06-30, composite_basis migration-seed, and the Article I, section 9 scope note.
Lens A records this match but does not evaluate treatment currency.
residual_risks: Treatment/currency is reserved for lens B.

reasons: The disclosed record identifies the case as an Oregon Supreme Court state case.

The lake scope note states that Mansor was decided under Article I, section 9 of the Oregon Constitution, not the Fourth Amendment, supporting the 'Persuasive — state, illustrative' label in this federal corpus.
residual_risks: The disclosed lake record does not contain a separate authority_weight field; this stands based on court identity and state-law scope.
